- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.5) and forecast is trending up, cap the rise at 1–2% above recent mean to prevent false momentum.  
- After a forecast spike, if true outcome shows a sharp drop, apply a 3–5 day lag correction to avoid premature reversal.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true mean over 3–5 days, apply a downward bias adjustment of 1–3% per day.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.3) and forecast is noisy, use a 3-day moving average to smooth out erratic peaks.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% in 2+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
